chunks: Sayf ibn Umayrah narrated to me, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

The mustahadah woman, when the days of her menstrual periods have passed, performs ghusl, inserts her cotton, and checks; if it appears on the cotton, she adds more cotton, performs wudu (ablution), and prays.

key_terms.أَيَّامُ أَقْرَائِهَا: the days of her habitual menstrual periods
key_terms.الْمُسْتَحَاضَةُ: a woman experiencing istihadah, irregular non-menstrual bleeding
key_terms.كُرْسُفَهَا: her cotton used to absorb and check the blood

ai.seo_question: What should a mustahadah woman do after her menstrual days have passed before performing salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for the mustahadah after the days of her usual menses have ended. It instructs her to perform ghusl, use cotton to manage the blood, inspect it, and if the blood appears on the cotton, to reinforce it, perform wudu (ablution), and then offer salat (prayer).
